0001| PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS & TEST SPECIFICATION
0002| Twilio Public Website
0003| www.twilio.com/en-us  —  anonymous (logged-out) experience only
0004| Field	Value
0005| Application under test	https://www.twilio.com/en-us (English, United States locale)
0006| Document type	Reverse-engineered PRD with an executable test suite
0007| Authentication	None. All requirements and test cases execute as an anonymous visitor.
0008| Environment	Public production site. No test credentials required or used.
0009| Baseline captured	September 11, 2026
0010| Owner	[QA Lead — TBD]
0011| Status	Draft v1.0 — for review
0012| 
0013| Scope constraint: no account credentials are available for this engagement. Every requirement and every test case in this document is verifiable without logging in. Anything behind authentication is listed in §3.2 as explicitly out of scope and has no test coverage here.
0014| 
0015| 
0016| 1. Purpose
0017| This document does two jobs. First, it states the requirements the Twilio public website is expected to satisfy, derived by inspecting the live site rather than from an internal specification. Second, it provides a test suite that a tester can execute end to end using nothing but a browser.
0018| It is written so that each requirement has at least one test case, and each test case traces back to a requirement. Section 12 holds the traceability matrix.
0019| 2. Product Overview
0020| Twilio sells communication and customer-engagement APIs. The public website is the top of the acquisition funnel: it explains the platform, routes visitors to the right product or solution page, and drives two conversion actions — starting a free trial and contacting sales.
0021| The homepage itself is a single long-scroll marketing page with a persistent global header. Its content sections are, in order: a hero with dual calls to action, a platform narrative in four parts, a product grid of six cards, a multi-language code sample block, a customer results carousel, an analyst recognition band, a closing conversion band, and a large footer with a sources accordion.
0022| 2.1 Primary visitor types
0023| Visitor	What they are trying to do	Success action
0024| Developer evaluator	Confirm the API can do the job and find the documentation quickly	Reaches docs or copies a code sample
0025| Technical buyer	Compare products, understand the platform, check pricing	Reaches a product or pricing page
0026| Enterprise buyer	Assess credibility, security posture, and analyst standing	Reaches customer stories or contacts sales
0027| Existing customer	Get to the console, the help centre, or the status page	Exits to the correct destination
0028| Job seeker / press / investor	Reach company information	Reaches the relevant footer destination
0029| 3. Scope
0030| 3.1 In scope
0031| - The English United States homepage and all global chrome rendered on it: utility bar, main navigation, mega menus, search entry point, and footer.
0032| - All homepage content sections and their interactive behaviour.
0033| - Link integrity for every outbound link reachable from the homepage, verified to the point of page load only.
0034| - Locale switching between the six published languages.
0035| - Responsive behaviour across desktop, tablet, and mobile breakpoints.
0036| - Accessibility, performance, and SEO characteristics of the homepage.
0037| - The unauthenticated state of any form reachable from the homepage — field presence, client-side validation, and error messaging — stopping short of submission.
0038| 3.2 Out of scope
0039| The following are excluded because they require credentials, create an account, or generate commercial contact. No test case in section 9 touches them.
0040| Excluded area	Reason
0041| Twilio Console (twilio.com/login) and anything after it	Requires account credentials
0042| SendGrid and Segment login destinations	Requires account credentials
0043| Free trial account creation — completing the sign-up at /try-twilio	Creates a real account and requires phone verification
0044| Contact sales form submission	Generates a real sales lead
0045| Webinar and gated asset registration	Creates a real registration record
0046| Newsletter or marketing consent submission	Creates a real subscription
0047| Any authenticated dashboard, billing, or usage view	Requires account credentials
0048| Backend API behaviour, message delivery, and telephony functionality	Not part of the website under test
0049| 
0050| Where a test case reaches a conversion form, the case ends at verifying the form renders and validates correctly. The submit action is never performed.
0051| 
0052| 
0053| 4. Page Inventory
0054| Destinations reachable from the homepage, grouped as the navigation groups them. Every one of these is publicly accessible.
0055| 4.1 Global chrome
0056| Element	Destinations
0057| Language selector	en-us, fr-fr, de-de, ja-jp, pt-br, es-mx
0058| Support menu	Help Center, Support Plans, Partner Solutions
0059| Login menu	Console, Segment, SendGrid — presence and link target only; not followed past the login screen
0060| Header actions	Contact sales, Start for free
0061| Search	Site search overlay with a privacy notice
0062| 4.2 Navigation groups

0064| Products	Twilio Platform, Conversations, Communications, Authentication, Customer Data	Conversation Memory, Conversation Orchestrator, Conversation Intelligence, Conversation Relay, Messaging, SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, Voice, SIP Trunking, Email, SMTP, Phone Numbers, Toll-free, 10DLC, Short Codes, Video, Flex, Verify, Lookup, Connections, Warehouses, Protocols, Unify, Engage, Audiences, Journeys
0065| Solutions	Use Cases, Teams, Industry, Company Size	Verification and identity, Fraud prevention, Alerts and notifications, Appointment reminders, Mass texting, Marketing and promotions, SMS marketing, Support and sales, Voice AI, IVR, Contact center, Developers, Marketing, Financial services, Healthcare, Retail, Nonprofit, Hospitality, Ecommerce, Public sector, Education, Enterprise, Startup
0066| Why Twilio	Overview, Differentiators, Company	Why Twilio, Customer stories, One platform, Trust center, Enterprise scale, Global infrastructure, About us, Values, Diversity, Careers, Twilio.org, Investor relations, Press, Events
0067| Resources	Developers, Learn, Support and services	Documentation, Code Exchange, Developer Hub, Champions, Changelog, Serverless, Blog, Resource Center, Guides, Reports, Webinars, Podcasts, State of Customer Engagement, Help Center, Partners, Professional services, Support plans, Status pages
0068| Pricing	Overview, Conversations, Communications, Authentication, Customer Data	All pricing, Messaging pricing, SMS pricing, WhatsApp pricing, Voice pricing, SIP Trunking pricing, Email API pricing, Video pricing, Flex pricing, Verify pricing, Lookup pricing, CDP pricing
0069| 5. Functional Requirements
0070| Requirement identifiers are used by the test cases in section 9 and the traceability matrix in section 12.
0071| 5.1 Global header and navigation
0072| ID	Requirement	Priority

0074| FR-NAV-02	The Twilio logo in the header links to the homepage and is present on every page reachable from it.	P0
0075| FR-NAV-03	Five top-level menus are present: Products, Solutions, Why Twilio, Resources, Pricing.	P0
0076| FR-NAV-04	Each top-level menu opens a mega menu on hover or click, and closes on outside click, on Escape, and when another menu opens.	P0
0077| FR-NAV-05	Every link inside every mega menu resolves to a live page returning HTTP 200 with no redirect chain longer than one hop.	P0
0078| FR-NAV-06	Mega menu contents are fully reachable and operable by keyboard alone, in a logical tab order.	P0
0079| FR-NAV-07	Both header conversion actions are present at all times: Contact sales and Start for free.	P0
0080| FR-NAV-08	The utility bar exposes a language selector listing six languages, a Support menu, and a Login menu.	P1
0081| FR-NAV-09	Selecting a language navigates to the equivalent localised path and the page renders in that language.	P0
0082| FR-NAV-10	The search control opens a search input and displays the associated data-collection notice with a link to the privacy policy.	P1
0083| FR-NAV-11	At viewports below the mobile breakpoint the navigation collapses to a toggle, and all menu groups remain reachable as expandable sections.	P0
0084| FR-NAV-12	Menu items flagged as new carry a visible badge, and promotional slots inside menus render their image, copy, and link.	P2
0085| 5.2 Homepage content

0090| FR-HOME-04	The product grid renders six cards: Conversations, Messaging, Email, Voice, User authentication, Customer data. Each card has an image, a heading, a description, and a link.	P0

0092| FR-HOME-06	The code sample block offers seven language tabs — Python, C#, PHP, Ruby, Java, JavaScript, cURL — and swaps the displayed sample without a page reload.	P0

0094| FR-HOME-08	The customer results carousel presents at least eight customer entries, each with a logo and a quantified result, and is advanceable by control, swipe, and keyboard.	P1

0098| FR-HOME-12	The closing conversion band repeats both primary actions, linking to the free trial and the pricing page.	P0

0100| FR-HOME-14	Images are served in a modern format with responsive sources, and offscreen images load lazily.	P1
0101| 5.3 Footer
0102| ID	Requirement	Priority
0103| FR-FOOT-01	The footer renders four collapsible link groups: Considering Twilio, Products and Features, Use Cases, Developers.	P0
0104| FR-FOOT-02	Legal and corporate links are present: Careers, Twilio.org, Press, Investor relations, Legal, Privacy, Security, Impressum, Sitemap.	P0
0105| FR-FOOT-03	Social links open in a new tab with appropriate rel attributes and accessible names.	P1

0107| FR-FOOT-05	The sitemap link resolves to a valid XML sitemap, and the machine-readable llms.txt resolves successfully.	P2

0109| 5.4 Conversion paths (render and validate only)
0110| ID	Requirement	Priority
0111| FR-CONV-01	Every Start for free control across the page leads to the free trial sign-up page and that page loads successfully.	P0
0112| FR-CONV-02	The sign-up page renders its expected fields and displays inline validation for empty, malformed, and disallowed input, without the form being submitted.	P0
0113| FR-CONV-03	Every Contact sales control leads to the sales contact page, which renders its form fields and validates them client-side.	P0
0114| FR-CONV-04	Campaign parameters present in the URL are preserved through navigation to the conversion page.	P2
0115| FR-CONV-05	Login menu entries point at the correct authentication destinations. Verification stops at the login screen rendering.	P1
0116| 6. Non-Functional Requirements
0117| ID	Area	Requirement
0118| NFR-01	Performance	Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5 s, Interaction to Next Paint under 200 ms, and Cumulative Layout Shift under 0.1, measured on a throttled mobile profile.
0119| NFR-02	Performance	The homepage becomes interactive without waiting on carousel or video assets; offscreen media is deferred.
0120| NFR-03	Accessibility	Conformance with WCAG 2.2 Level AA. No critical or serious violations from an automated scan, plus a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass.
0121| NFR-04	Accessibility	Visible focus indicator on every interactive element; no keyboard trap in menus, carousels, or accordions.
0122| NFR-05	Accessibility	Text contrast at least 4.5:1, and large text and interface components at least 3:1.
0123| NFR-06	Responsive	Correct rendering at 360, 768, 1024, 1440, and 1920 pixels wide, with no horizontal scrolling and no overlapping content.
0124| NFR-07	Compatibility	Current and previous major versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge, plus Safari on iOS and Chrome on Android.
0125| NFR-08	SEO	A single H1, a unique title and meta description, a canonical tag, Open Graph and Twitter card metadata, and hreflang alternates for all six locales.
0126| NFR-09	SEO	No broken internal links, no soft 404s, and a valid robots directive permitting indexing of the homepage.
0127| NFR-10	Security	Site served over HTTPS with a valid certificate; HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS; security headers present.
0128| NFR-11	Privacy	Consent mechanism appears where required by the visitor region, and analytics tags respect the recorded choice.
0129| NFR-12	Reliability	No uncaught JavaScript errors in the console and no failed network requests on a clean page load.
0130| NFR-13	Localisation	Each locale renders translated content with correct character encoding and no untranslated placeholder strings.
0131| NFR-14	Analytics	The tag manager container loads and fires a page-view event; conversion controls emit their tracking events.
0132| 7. Test Approach
0133| 7.1 Method
0134| - Manual exploratory and scripted execution for layout, content, and interaction.
0135| - Automated link crawling for the link-integrity cases, limited to a depth of one from the homepage.
0136| - Automated accessibility scanning with axe or an equivalent, followed by a manual keyboard pass, because automated tools catch roughly a third of real issues.
0137| - Lighthouse and WebPageTest for the performance cases, run three times with the median taken.
0138| - Browser developer tools for console errors, network failures, and response headers.
0139| 7.2 Test data
0140| No credentials are used. Form validation cases use synthetic input only, and no form is ever submitted. Suggested invalid inputs: an empty string, a single space, an address missing the at sign, an address with a trailing dot, a 300-character string, a script tag, and a SQL fragment. These exercise client-side validation without creating records.
0141| 7.3 Entry and exit criteria
0142| Gate	Criteria
0143| Entry	The site is reachable, the test environment browsers are installed, and the baseline screenshots from the capture date are available.
0144| Exit	All P0 cases executed with no open critical or high defects; at least 95% of P1 cases executed; all deviations documented.
0145| 7.4 Defect severity
0146| Severity	Definition	Example
0147| Critical	A conversion path or the navigation is unusable	Start for free leads to a 404
0148| High	Major function broken with no workaround	A mega menu will not open on a supported browser
0149| Medium	Function impaired but a workaround exists	Carousel arrows fail but swipe works
0150| Low	Cosmetic or content issue	Inconsistent spacing in a footer column
0151| 
0152|

0363| 11. Assumptions and Risks
0364| - The site is a live production property owned by a third party. Content and layout can change without notice, so any content-matching case should be re-baselined before a regression run.
0365| - Marketing sites commonly run A/B tests. A tester may see a variant that differs from the captured baseline; treat a difference as a possible experiment before raising a defect.
0366| - Geolocation affects the consent banner and some pricing content. Record the test location with each result.
0367| - Link-integrity crawling should be rate-limited to avoid being treated as abusive traffic.
0368| - Because no account exists, roughly the entire authenticated product surface is untested. If console coverage is later required, a separate specification and a test account will be needed.
